claim.pdf_says: EXPANDS | class-specifier and interface-specifier of the REPOSITORY paragraph
claim.markdown_says:
| EXPANDS | class-specifier and interface-specifier of the REPOSITORY |

paragraph

| FOREGROUND-COLOR | screen description entry |
claim.why_it_matters: The wrapped second line of the EXPANDS context cell is detached from the table as a stray paragraph 'paragraph', so the EXPANDS row's context reads 'of the REPOSITORY' with no noun and the table is split in two.

verdict.reasoning: Printed page 141 (PDF p163), §2002:8.10 table: the EXPANDS row's context cell reads 'class-specifier and interface-specifier of the REPOSITORY' and wraps to 'paragraph' on the next line inside the same cell. The transcription (page-163.md lines 24-29) closes the EXPANDS row after 'REPOSITORY', emits 'paragraph' as a standalone paragraph outside the table, then restarts a new table whose first row is '| FOREGROUND-COLOR | screen description entry |' followed by '|---|---|'. Both quotes in the claim match the sources. The word is not lost, but this is more than a wrapping difference: the table's structure is broken. A reader of the markdown table gets an EXPANDS context with no noun, and in GFM the FOREGROUND-COLOR row becomes the header row of a second table, so any tool that reads the context-sensitive-word table by rows drops FOREGROUND-COLOR as a data row and loses 'paragraph' from EXPANDS. This is a genuine structural transcription defect, not a normative change to the standard's meaning.
verdict.corrected_description: Accurate as stated, with one addition: because the table restarts after the stray 'paragraph' line, the '|---|---|' separator follows the FOREGROUND-COLOR row, so FOREGROUND-COLOR is promoted to the header row of a second table rather than being a data row. Fix: put 'paragraph' back into the EXPANDS context cell and join the two tables into one.
